title: Design System: Ledgendary audience pages (v4 "Episodes")
scope: site-v4/ only (look v4 alternate). Not a project-wide system; site/, site-v2/, site-v3/ and later looks are competing alternates in their own worlds. Derived from site-v4/styles.css, the four HTML pages and app.js as finished 2026-11-19 after the finish review and two fix rounds. Values are the final cascaded ones (the stylesheet appends late override blocks for the finale and frame labels).

display.purpose: The audience headline in the hero, two stacked lines.

title-card-big.purpose: One episode per page; words set in one by one.

title-card.purpose: Every other episode heading, code and title on one line.

episode-code.purpose: 'S01E04 ·' inside the title card heading, tabular.

headline.purpose: The special and the finale headings.

lede.purpose: Title card ledes and the special lede; the hero subline runs 1.25rem/1.42 in ink-2.

wink.purpose: Italic heavy aside under a title card; 1.375rem on the big card.

figure.purpose: Big numbers in recap and finale frames.

label.purpose: Chips, tags, index pins, table heads; sentence case.

shadows.name: window
shadows.purpose: Product windows, the current recap frame, hovered season rows.

shadows.name: small
shadows.purpose: The waitlist field; the current recap frame on phones.

shadows.name: button-hover
shadows.purpose: Primary button hover, with a 1px rise.

shadows.name: focus-ring-field
shadows.purpose: Waitlist field focus-within (peach #ffd0b5 on error), layered over the small shadow.

motion.name: hover
motion.purpose: Hover and press on buttons, links, icon buttons.

motion.name: state-swap

motion.name: title-wipe
motion.purpose: Ordinary title cards wipe in left to right.

motion.name: stamp
motion.purpose: Paid stamp lands from -12deg, 1.5x scale and blur.

motion.name: beat

narrative.overview:
A white page that reads like a season of a sitcom, told in type and product. Every signature feature is an episode: a soft colour field with large rounded corners carrying a heavy, tight title card ("S01E04 · The Late Fee Incident") and, beneath it, a white product window outlined in ink that plays the feature in beats. The episode code sits on the same heading line as the title at a lighter weight, so the title card is one statement rather than a label over a heading. There is no TV imagery anywhere: no screens, no remotes, no frames styled as television. The streaming-title craft lives entirely in type and timing.

Four pastel fields carry meaning, not decoration: peach for proposals and clients, sky for time and people, mint for getting paid, lilac for the books and trust. They tint the episode fields, the index pins once seen, avatars, chips and the soft notes inside windows. One hot colour, tomato, is reserved for the action and for Paid, and it always carries ink text. Ink (near-black) draws everything structural at 1.5px: window outlines, chip rings, the window bar's rule, table head rules, the nav's scrolled rule.

The hero opens on white with a huge two-line audience headline, a subline, the waitlist field and a quiet "Season 1 · 8 episodes" line, then a "Previously on…" strip of five live frames that autoplay with a segmented progress bar and pause. On desktop a sticky season index runs beside the episodes, tracking progress and jumping between them. The page closes on a "No handoffs" special and a finale box that repeats the waitlist beside a recap of the season.
keyCharacteristics: White ground; colour arrives as large rounded episode fields, one role per field.
Ink at 1.5px draws every outline; product windows are white, ink-outlined and softly lifted.
Tomato only for the action and Paid, always under ink text.
Gabarito alone, 400 to 900; display at 900 and tight, the episode code at 500 on the same line.
Every product surface carries a dashed "Demo data" tag and plays its feature in numbered beats.

rules.name: The One Field, One Role Rule
rules.body: Peach is proposals and clients, sky is time and people, mint is getting paid, lilac is the books and trust. An episode takes the field of its subject, and every tint inside it follows the same mapping.

rules.name: The Tomato Is Action and Paid Rule
rules.body: Tomato fills the one action a visitor or a demo user takes and the moment money lands. It carries ink, never white, and it is never a field, a border or text.

rules.name: The Code On The Line Rule
rules.body: The episode code and the episode title are one heading: code at 500, title at 900, separated by a middle dot. Nothing sits above a title card.

rules.name: The Tabular Columns Rule
rules.body: Money, durations, figures, table cells, hashes, chain rows, timestamps and episode codes carry tabular numerals; running copy does not.

rules.name: The Ink Line Rule
rules.body: Structure is a 1.5px ink line; 1px `hair` only divides rows. Fields carry no outline at all: their colour is the edge.

dos: Do give every episode one field from its subject: peach proposals and clients, sky time and people, mint getting paid, lilac books and trust.
Do draw structure with a 1.5px ink line and keep product windows white with the soft window shadow.
Do set the episode code and title on one heading line, code at 500 and title at 900.
Do use tomato only for the action and for Paid, always with ink text.
Do tag every product surface with the dashed "Demo data" tag and play it in numbered, pausable beats.
Do set money, durations and figures in tabular numerals.
Do give every animated piece a finished resting state under reduced motion and without JavaScript.
donts: Don't use TV imagery (screens, remotes, broadcast frames) or name a show; the season is told in type.
Don't put a label or kicker above a title card; the code belongs on the title's line.
Don't put white text on tomato, or use tomato as text, border or field.
Don't lay a field colour on its own field; inside a field use white windows and the soft twins inside them.
Don't use hard offset shadows, glow or glass; lift is soft and reserved for windows, the current frame and the primary button.
Don't add a second display family or a system display face; Gabarito carries everything.
